title: Next.js App Router Migration Error

structured_notes.concern: The STUDENT experienced broken navigation links (404 errors) while upgrading a project to the new App router.
structured_notes.action_taken: The TEACHER reviewed the folder structure and identified a misunderstanding of the new directory-based routing conventions.
structured_notes.outcome: The STUDENT learned that route files must be named `page.js` inside designated folders, and that components can now safely co-exist in the app directory.
structured_notes.remarks: The STUDENT needs to adapt to the new framework patterns. Restructuring the folders will immediately fix the 404 errors.

reference_transcript:
Teacher: How is the code update for your project going, Alex?
Student: It is difficult. I am trying to move from the old Next.js Pages router to the new App router. Now, my navigation links are completely broken.
Teacher: The new App router changes how folders work. Show me your folder structure right now.
Student: I moved my 'about.js' file into the new 'app' folder, but going to the '/about' URL in my browser gives a 404 error.
Teacher: In the App router, the folder name becomes the path, not the file name. You need to make a folder named 'about' and put a file named 'page.js' inside it.
Student: Oh, so the file must always be named 'page.js' to work as a page?
Teacher: Yes, for it to be a public route. The same goes for your other pages. Your 'contact.js' should become a folder named 'contact' with a 'page.js' inside.
Student: What happens if I have components like a navigation bar? Can they stay in the app folder?
Teacher: Yes, you can place components in the app folder now. Only files named 'page.js' or 'route.js' become accessible URLs. Everything else is ignored by the router.
Student: That makes the file structure much cleaner. I will reorganize the folders now. Thanks for clarifying that.
reference_summary: The STUDENT struggled with 404 errors after moving files to the new App router. The TEACHER explained the new folder-based routing system requiring `page.js` files. The STUDENT will reorganize the project directory to fix the navigation.
